newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France head briefs Jospin.
newsitem.headline: Air France head briefs Jospin.

text.p: The chairman of state-owned Air France, Christian Blanc, briefed Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Monday on the situation at the flag carrier but gave no details on any hopes of an early privatisation.
"Mr Jospin is a man whom I have known for a long time and I gave a very long and precise presentation of the situation at Air France," the airline executive told reporters after the meeting.
"We had a very rigorous, very methodical, and I hope very useful, meeting," he added.

Blanc has consistently called for a speedy sell-off of Air France, which has received 20 billion francs in public money over the last three years in return for a restructuring plan and an eventual privatisation.

The new government has not yet taken a position on that sell-off, which was agreed with the European Commission by the previous French conservative administration. No date was set for the privatisation other than that the company should have returned to profit.
Air France posted a net consolidated profit of 394 million francs for 1996/97 on May 29, its first net surplus since 1989.
Communist transport minister Jean-Claude Gayssot has previously said he prefers a public sector solution.

Blanc dismissed French newspaper reports which said there could be a trade-off between dropping the Air France privatisation in exchange for building a third runway at Charles-De-Gaulle Paris airport, which is the airline's international hub. "It's an invention," Blanc said.
